title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Between visits of the head the tape is a word over the two letters 1 and 10 (no two 0s side by side). Each sweep acts on it like one generation of a cellular automaton whose patterns look random. The run proceeds in waves: a chaotic region spreads from the left end across the whole tape and freezes behind a slower front; each wave starts with three quick bursts of growth at the left end. Successive waves take about 3.06 times longer. The bbchallenge wiki lists it as "chaotic 1dCA in bell"; the same table started in states C, D, E, F is four other holdouts.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 53,911 cells have been visited and 42,422 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The sweeps cross blocks of ones
claims.text: C crosses 1^n to the right in 3n steps (carrying the 0 behind it), E crosses it to the left in n steps: only the isolated 0s take work.

claims.title: No 00 inside the tape
claims.text: At all 25,729 visits of the head to the right end in state B up to 3·108 steps, the tape has no two adjacent 0s outside its last three cells: it is a word over 1 and 10.

claims.title: Waves about 3.06 times longer each
claims.text: The left end grows in triples of bursts that start at steps 643294, 2108809, 6495092, 20126119, 60650898, 187352297, 570905460, 1767969175: ratios 3.28, 3.08, 3.10, 3.01, 3.09, 3.05, 3.10. The tape width at those moments grows by about 1.75 = √3.06 each time.

claims.title: Same table, other start states
claims.text: Started in C, D, E or F (and renamed to normal form) this table is the holdout 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD, 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA, 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE or 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF; the wiki notes that they all behave alike.

claims.title: Halting looks like a matter of chance
claims.text: Each wave ends with the chaotic content reaching the left end, where a halt (A reading 1) could happen. If the content arriving there were random with a fixed small chance p per wave of being a halting one, the machine would halt after about 1/p waves, i.e. after roughly 3.06<sup>1/p</sup> steps: a halt would be likely eventually but unobservably late. Whether any reachable left-end content halts is not known.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.07). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Next step: Extract the cellular automaton (the map from the word over {1, 10} before a sweep to the word after), then study the left-end boundary rule: which contents can make A read 1 there.

The same table as 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine runs a chaotic cellular automaton on its own tape: each sweep of the head is one generation. Chaos spreads over the tape in waves, each about three times longer than the last.

facts.text: Each wave lasts about 3.06 times as long as the previous one.
The tape is a word over these two letters, no 00 inside.
No halt in the C simulator; 53,911 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A cellular automaton in waves
html:
Whenever the head reaches the right end, the tape contains no 00 (except next to the head): it is a sequence of the letters 1 and 10. The head crosses runs of 1s quickly and does real work only at the 0s, so a sweep acts like one generation of a cellular automaton on this sequence, and the patterns it makes look random.

The run goes in waves. A chaotic region (the speckled triangles) starts at the left end and spreads right to the growing end of the tape; behind it a front moves right and leaves a frozen pattern (vertical lines). Each wave begins when the left end grows in three quick bursts; the next wave starts before the front of the previous one has reached the right end. Each wave lasts about 3.06 times as long as the previous one:

A halt needs A to read a 1, which in practice means the right content arriving at the left end. With chaotic content, a halt would be a matter of chance per wave; since waves grow geometrically, even a likely halt could come impossibly late.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.07). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503).
After 109 steps the tape spans 53,911 cells (151 left of the start, 35,882 right), with a density of 1s of 0.787.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF: rename A→C, B→D, C→B, D→E, E→F, F→A and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state F, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA: rename A→E, B→F, C→D, D→A, E→B, F→C and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE: rename A→D, B→E, C→C, D→F, E→A, F→B and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror

family: Chaotic one-dimensional cellular automaton in growing bursts ("chaotic 1dCA in bell")
summary: Emulates a chaotic one-dimensional cellular automaton on words of 1 and 10: chaos spreads over the tape in waves, each about 3.06 times longer than the last; a halt (A reading 1) needs the right pattern at the slow left end.
